prompt_preview:
Read-only planning specialist. Give one actionable plan, risks and a bounded falsifying test; do not edit files.
Read-only bounded Rust architecture plan in /home/rb/worktrees/borsuk-prod-ready-v9. Use Git objects at origin/main 3b70a8e3b863cca220ce1c15df5ac363f9e0aec3; physical checkout is stale dirty, do not edit/reset. Read docs/research/performance-architecture-20260930/cohere1024/leaf-metric-coverage-screen-a0001/{decision.md,layer-reconciliation.md,human-summary.json if present}, docs/research/next-route-research-20260928/fable-result.md, and relevant generic Rust graph/layout/router implementations. Current Cohere1M D1024 k10 consumed32 original returned313/320, SOURCE scored coverage314/320; six omissions proved first lost layer leaf nomination. Cosine48 screen measured312/320, gained0 lost2: rejected, no rerun/count sweep. Historical Fable proposes source-row-kNN cut-edge page adjacency without copies; historical centroid hierarchies/copy arms rejected on other data, cannot transfer scores. Determine ONE concrete distinct generic Rust nomination intervention leveraging existing code (prefer boundary adjacency only if feasible); identify required source inputs, existing reusable APIs, exact smallest implementation files, resource/build envelope estimates distinguished from measurements, and cheap native correctness/recall falsifier. Explain why distinct from rejected centroid hierarchies and what evidence would reject it. If current source/data cannot support it, say exact missing prerequisite and choose smallest justified alternative, not a new reporting framework. No native/Cargo/tests/mocks/data parsing/network/cloud/children/edits. Source/Git reads only, <=CPU1/256MiB bounded reads, no broad cache scans. Operator substantive Rust only; all future native execution causality EC2. Provide concise actionable plan, not implementation.

active_goal.objective: Ship a production-ready, self-contained Rust BORSUK ANN library on S3/blob storage that beats BOTH S3 Vectors and Turbopuffer at equal or better recall on matched end-to-end p90/p95 latency and throughput per total dollar. This is a product goal, not a report. Support incremental insert/update/delete, authenticated generation-pinned publication and reads, bounded RAM/cache/concurrency, restart/recovery, and in-process automatic or callable compaction/GC; require no separate maintenance instance. Preserve current V282 on-demand SQ8 work and live jobs; do not duplicate consultations or paid runs. Opus 5.5 estimates the current PQ64 plus f32 summary/unit router at 184 resident bytes per row, or about 18.4 GB at 100M D768, before old-generation pinning. This is a projection, not a measurement. Reconcile prior V139/V146/V149/V150 centroid-page failures and the completed Fable review before choosing any new arm; do not repeat a known failure. Predeclare a feasible 100M RAM, GET, byte, p90 and cost envelope. Prefer a small resident router and one parallel S3 fetch wave, but choose memory versus quality from a measured Pareto curve, not an arbitrary 2 GB cap. Candidate design: balanced hierarchical semantic cells with physical locality and boundary coverage; scan small SQ8 leaves, split skewed/diffuse leaves, use local compressed indexing only where measured cell-specific gains justify it. Avoid S3 graph pointer chasing and full-vector/full-graph hydration. First run the cheapest distinct paired 100k D768 cosine k100 falsifier on ReLAION and CoHere against unchanged V282, decomposing exact-GT loss into router, selected-cell coverage, local index and SQ8 quantization and counting GETs, bytes, RAM and route CPU. Use V282 98% mean recall@100, p05 95, 32 GET and 16 MiB caps unless a redesign is predeclared; kill weak arms early. Freeze a winner for fresh 1M cold HTTP, then 10M and 100M scale. Measure p50/p90/p95/p99, QPS, RSS including generation swap, physical S3 requests/bytes/retries/errors, build and incremental-maintenance cost, total lifecycle cost and failure recovery. Compare competitors on identical corpus, query split, metric, k, filters, cache state, region and concurrency; if only published targets are available, cite date/configuration and label mismatches, never claim a measured win. When a gate fails, redesign routing, layout, quantization or fetch schedule with one causal change per experiment. Unreleased formats need no backward compatibility. Push code, tests, receipts and a concise decision table to BORSUK main. Within 24 hours deliver one substantive object-native library increment and a falsifiable next gate, then continue until the product works.
active_goal.note: re-apply delivery failed; prior goal state restored

partial_result:
Recommend **one sampled SQ8 row boundary-adjacency arm over the existing semantic leaves**, keeping the 48-leaf budget and physical layout fixed. Plan against Git revision `3b70a8e3b863cca220ce1c15df5ac363f9e0aec3`.

The six SOURCE coverage omissions are established leaf-nomination losses. Fable’s full FP32 row-kNN layout needs prerequisites absent from the inspected screen inventory: authenticated canonical FP32 rows and a same-source row-neighbor graph, or a qualified graph build. The inventory already admits SQ8 rows, calibration and membership, so the smaller arm below is executable without obtaining another vector representation.

1. **Construct adjacency without queries or truth.** Stream and authenticate the existing SQ8 object, generation, plane, router root and membership. Verify physical-ID order against `native_order_sha256`. Select one actual reconstructed row per 32-row unit at physical position `min(32u+16, N−1)`; decode with authenticated `low/step`, normalize, and label it with `membership[u]`. Admit dimensions explicitly within the existing 1–1024 ceiling.

2. **Project sampled row edges onto leaves.** Reuse `centroid_hnsw::build_hnsw_adjacency` with fixed `m=16`, `m0=32`, construction/search width 64. Despite the helper’s name, its inputs here are individual reconstructed rows. Count cross-leaf base edges; retain each leaf’s top 16 neighbors by count, ties by leaf ID. Drop sampled vectors and the row graph after construction. This is approximate adjacency over sampled SQ8 rows—not full-source exact kNN.

3. **Replace nomination once, without a sweep.** Keep the first 40 leaves from the original L2 ranking. Fill eight positions from their adjacency using descending votes  
   `Σ (40 − seed_rank) × cut_edge_count`.  
   Break ties by original L2 rank, then leaf ID; fill shortages from the remaining original ranking. Pass the 48 distinct IDs through existing `nominate_selected`. SOURCE closure, scoring and cover limits stay fixed.

4. **Limit the implementation to two files for this screen.**
   - `crates/borsuk/src/semantic_unit_router.rs`: generic adjacency construction, authenticated decoding and boundary selection, with tests in the existing module. Use a separate versioned adjacency artifact bound to generation/root/membership/SQ8/order identities.
   - `crates/borsuk/examples/compare_native_replay.rs`: bounded streaming construction and a distinct candidate entrypoint, reusing `coverage_router`, producer-control parity, selection sealing, `loss_positions` and the existing cover planner. Preserve historical cosine-arm behavior and receipts.

**Bounded falsifier:** On causality Spot EC2, first test deterministic edges/ties, duplicate and corrupt identities, short final units, and dimension rejection. Then perform source-bound admission and a separate disposable smoke. Freeze the single arm, construct adjacency with requests/truth unopened, and durably seal paired original/candidate nominations before opening truth.

Require the original control to reproduce **returned313/320 and SOURCE coverage314/320**. Reject this arm if candidate SOURCE-scored coverage is below **315/320**, or if it loses any previously covered slot. Count owning nominated units, not fetched gap bridges. Protocol/setup errors are INVALID; preserve them separately. No parameter sweep follows rejection. Survival only licenses returned-recall qualification.

**Proposed envelopes, not measurements:** 31,250 sampled D1024 f32 rows occupy approximately **122 MiB**; graph and edge-count scratch should keep modeled construction below **256 MiB**. Preregister CPU1, RSS512 MiB, swap0, a 900-second construction deadline and 2 GiB staging disk. Adjacency costs at most `128 × leaf_count` bytes plus offsets/header—roughly **0.1 MB** for this root. Query expansion examines at most 640 links. Separately budget remote compilation at two compiler jobs, 16 GiB RAM and 64 GiB build disk; run affected targets, required workspace Clippy and `scripts/check_rust_test_build.sh` before handoff.

This differs from rejected centroid hierarchies because boundary evidence comes from individual rows, with no new mean hierarchy or row replication. Sampling can miss rare boundaries; cut counts can favor large leaves; replacements can scatter closure pages and exceed existing cover caps. Historical ReLAION scores provide no Cohere prediction.

Git/source reads only; no edits, native execution, data parsing, network, cloud actions or children.
A failed screen rejects this sampled SQ8 arm, not every FP32 boundary-adjacency design; survival establishes no latency or vendor win.
